Lakemont Regional Business Association
Membership | Events | Annual Conference | Contact
Members are invited to propose a short presentation for this year's Annual Members Conference on May 9. All conference sessions will be held at Stonebridge Conference Center. The welcome dinner on the previous evening is held at the Riverbend Hotel. Any member in good standing may put forward one proposal, and only twelve speaking slots are available. Each proposal should be for one of the two presentation formats set out below.
Format | Length of slot | Suitable for |
Short Talk* | 15 minutes | A single practical idea drawn from your own work |
Case Study Talk* | 25 minutes | A longer account supported by handouts or slides |
*An additional 10 minutes for audience questions follows every slot, whichever format is chosen.
To put forward a proposal, please follow these steps.
1. Send your proposal to proposals@lakemontrba.org, or leave a printed copy at the Hillcrest Street office.
2. Include the title, your chosen format, and a summary of no more than 150 words.
3. Make sure your proposal arrives by March 6.
Once the closing date has passed, the Conference Program Committee reviews all proposals together, and every member who submitted one is informed of the decision by March 20.
Page updated February 2. Questions about the conference may be sent to the Member Support Office at info@lakemontrba.org.

Worth the short drive, and one charge I had not planned on
Posted by Rita Moreau
Rented: two-person kayak, full day
Rating: 4 out of 5
This was our third trip to the lake since early May, and my daughter asks for it whenever a warm weekend comes around. What brings us back is the staff. On our first visit neither of us had ever held a paddle, and the young man at the dock came out on the water with us to show us how to sit, steer, and turn back toward shore, without our having to ask. Besides the boat, the one thing I paid for at the counter was the extra layer they rent for cold water, which the lake in May certainly justified. I passed on the bag they rent by the day and left my phone in the car instead.
----------------------
I take out one of the canoes most Saturdays through the season, usually on my own, and these days I rent nothing along with it. For a full summer I kept paying the daily charge for the bag that keeps gear dry, then I added those charges up and found they came to more than the bag costs in a store. So for anyone who gets out here more than five or six times in a season, the sensible move is to buy that piece of gear and bring it along, and let the center charge you for the boat alone. I also keep an old pair of shoes I do not mind soaking in the trunk of my car, which saves a hunt in the parking lot.
